Here it is for 6 servings:

- 1200 g chicken thighs
- 1050 g sweet potatoes
- 900 g sweetcorn
- 3 tbsp olive oil
- 2.25 tsp salt
- 1.5 tsp black pepper
- 1.5 tsp paprika
- 1.5 tsp garlic powder
- 180 ml ketchup
- 3 tbsp brown sugar
- 1.5 tbsp cider vinegar
- 1.5 tsp mustard
- 3 tbsp water

Method:
1. Heat the oven to 220°C. Line a large baking tray with baking paper if you have it.
2. Cut the sweet potatoes into bite-sized chunks. Toss them with 1 tablespoon olive oil, 1/2 teaspoon salt, and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper. Spread them on the tray and roast for 15 minutes.
3. Meanwhile, mix the ketchup, brown sugar, cider vinegar, mustard, water, paprika, garlic powder, and a pinch of salt in a bowl to make the barbecue sauce.
4. Pat the chicken thighs dry, season with the remaining salt and pepper, then toss with the barbecue sauce until well coated.
5. Remove the tray from the oven, add the sweetcorn and chicken thighs, and turn the sweet potatoes. Drizzle the sweetcorn with the remaining olive oil.
6. Return to the oven and roast for 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through, the juices run clear, and the sweet potatoes are browned at the edges.
7. If you want a stickier glaze, brush the chicken with any extra sauce and roast for 3 to 5 minutes more. Serve the chicken with the roasted sweet potato and sweetcorn.

Baking soda and baking powder are both leavening agents, but they work differently:

- **Baking soda** = pure sodium bicarbonate. It needs an **acid** in the batter or dough to make gas and help things rise. Examples of acids: yogurt, buttermilk, lemon juice, vinegar, brown sugar, cocoa powder.
- **Baking powder** = baking soda **plus** an acid already built in, so it can rise with just moisture and heat. Most baking powder is **double-acting**, meaning it starts working when mixed and again in the oven.

Quick rule:
- Use **baking soda** when the recipe already has an acidic ingredient.
- Use **baking powder** when it doesn’t.

Too much can affect taste:
- **Baking soda** can taste bitter or soapy if overused.
- **Baking powder** can leave a metallic or chemical taste if there’s too much.

If you want, I can also give you a simple substitution guide between the two.

Here’s a chocolate cake recipe:

**Ingredients**
- 250 g plain flour
- 200 g sugar
- 50 g cocoa powder
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1 pinch salt
- 2 eggs
- 240 ml milk
- 120 ml vegetable oil
- 2 tsp vanilla extract
- 240 ml hot water
- 75 g butter
- 150 g icing sugar
- 25 g cocoa powder
- 2 tbsp milk

**Method**
- Heat the oven to 175°C and grease and line a 20 cm cake tin or two sandwich tins.
- Mix the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
- Whisk in the eggs, milk, oil, and vanilla until smooth.
- Stir in the hot water; the batter will be thin.
- Pour into the tin or tins and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
- Cool completely before frosting.
- Beat the butter with the icing sugar and cocoa powder, then add the milk to make a spreadable frosting.
- Spread over the cooled cake.

Here’s a chocolate cake recipe for you:

**Egg-Free Chocolate Cake**  
**Servings:** 8  
**Time:** 50 min

**Ingredients**
- 250 g plain flour
- 200 g sugar
- 50 g cocoa powder
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1 pinch salt
- 120 ml vegetable oil
- 240 ml water
- 2 tsp vanilla extract
- 1 tbsp white vinegar
- 100 g dark chocolate
- 120 ml coconut milk
- 150 g powdered sugar

**Method**
- Heat the oven to 180°C and grease or line a round cake tin.
- Mix the flour, sugar, cocoa powder, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
- Stir in the oil, water, vanilla extract, and vinegar until smooth.
- Pour the batter into the tin and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
- Cool the cake in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a rack and cool fully.
- For the frosting, melt the dark chocolate gently, then stir in the coconut milk and powdered sugar until smooth.
- Spread the frosting over the cooled cake and serve.

Classic Beef Lasagne

Ingredients for 4 servings:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion
- 1 carrot
- 1 celery stick
- 2 garlic cloves
- 500 g beef mince
- 2 tbsp tomato puree
- 800 g chopped tomatoes
- 250 ml beef stock
- 1 tsp dried oregano
- 1 tsp dried basil
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 50 g butter
- 50 g plain flour
- 600 ml milk
- 1 pinch nutmeg
- 12 lasagne sheets
- 50 g parmesan
- 150 g mozzarella

Method:
- Heat the oven to 190°C. Finely chop the onion, carrot, celery, and garlic.
- Heat the olive oil in a large pan and cook the onion, carrot, and celery for 6 to 8 minutes until softened. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
- Add the beef mince and cook until browned, breaking it up as it cooks.
- Stir in the tomato puree, chopped tomatoes, beef stock, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 20 to 25 minutes until thickened.
- Meanwhile, make the béchamel: melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour, and cook for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk until smooth. Cook until thick and creamy, then season with nutmeg, salt, and pepper.
- Spread a thin layer of meat sauce in a baking dish. Add a layer of lasagne sheets, then more meat sauce, then béchamel. Repeat, finishing with béchamel on top.
- Scatter over the parmesan and mozzarella.
- Bake for 30 to 35 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

I don’t have a banana bread recipe in the current recipe set, so here’s a simple one you can make at home.

**Banana Bread**  
Makes 1 loaf

**Ingredients**
- 3 ripe bananas
- 75 g butter
- 150 g sugar
- 2 eggs
- 1 tsp vanilla extract
- 190 g plain flour
- 1 tsp baking soda
- 1/2 tsp salt
- 1 tsp cinnamon
- 60 g chopped walnuts or chocolate chips, optional

**Method**
- Heat the oven to 175°C and grease or line a loaf tin.
- Mash the bananas in a bowl.
- Stir in the melted butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla.
- In another bowl, mix the flour, baking soda, salt, and cinnamon.
- Add the dry ingredients to the banana mixture and stir just until combined.
- Fold in walnuts or chocolate chips, if using.
- Pour into the loaf tin and bake for 50 to 60 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean.
- Cool in the tin for 10 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool fully.

Here’s your revised recipe draft:

**Spinach, Tomato, Broccoli, and Tofu Pasta Salad**  
Makes 2 servings

**Ingredients**
- 180 g pasta
- 200 g tofu
- 2 cups spinach
- 1 cup cherry tomatoes
- 1 cup broccoli florets
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 1 tsp Dijon mustard
- 1 tsp garlic powder
- 1 pinch salt
- 1 pinch black pepper

**Steps**
- Cook the pasta in salted water until tender, then drain and rinse under cold water.
- Steam or boil the broccoli for 2 to 3 minutes until bright green and just tender, then cool it briefly.
- Cut the tofu into cubes and pan-fry it in a little oil until lightly golden on all sides.
- Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, mustard, garlic powder, salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
- In a large bowl, combine the pasta, spinach, cherry tomatoes, broccoli, and tofu.
- Pour over the dressing and toss well.
- Serve chilled or at room temperature.

Here’s a milder version with sweet potato:

Spicy Lentil Soup, Mild with Sweet Potato

Makes 4 servings.

Ingredients:
- 2 tbsp olive oil
- 1 onion
- 2 carrots
- 2 celery stalks
- 4 garlic cloves
- 1 small sweet potato
- 1/2 tsp red chili flakes
- 2 tsp ground cumin
- 1 tsp smoked paprika
- 250 g brown lentils
- 400 g canned diced tomatoes
- 1 l vegetable broth
- 1 tsp salt
- 1/2 tsp black pepper
- 1 tbsp lemon juice
- 2 tbsp fresh parsley

Steps:
- Heat the olive oil in a pot over medium heat.
- Add the onion, carrot, celery, and sweet potato, and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring often.
- Stir in the garlic, chili flakes, cumin, and smoked paprika, and cook for 30 seconds.
- Add the lentils, tomatoes, vegetable broth, salt, and black pepper.
- Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer and cook until the lentils and sweet potato are tender, about 25 to 30 minutes.
- Stir in the lemon juice and parsley.
- Taste and adjust the seasoning, then serve hot.
